question.problem:
The table below gives some values of a continuous function $f(t)$ on the closed interval $[10,40].$ The right Riemann sum approximation to the area under the curve $y=f(t)$ with $3$ equal subintervals has a value of $480.$ What must be the value of $k?$

| $t$ | $10$ | $20$ | $30$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(t)$ | $18$ | $12$ | $k$ | $16$ |
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(20)+f(30)+f(40)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $20$ | $30$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(t)$ | $12$ | $k$ | $16$ |

So, we obtain the following approximation to the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(12+k+16)\cdot 10 \\  & =(28+k)\cdot 10\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are given that $A$ must be $480$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(28+k)\cdot 10 & =480 \\ 28+k & =48 \\ k & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
